The Petitioner has filed the Petition against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation Rs.50,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in Petition are as under:
That on 11.02.2022 at about 11.30 a.m. the petitioner was riding two wheeler bearing No.KA-01-HV-2674 near Haraluru lake dew Residence Society, 16th Main Road towards Anjeneyaswamy temple road, Bangalore, at that time, the driver of Maruti Swift Dezire car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AC- 4417 came in a rash and negligent manner, tried to over take the scooter from the extreme left side which was not permissible under law and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle.
Due to this impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to head and all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Manipal hospital,
wherein she was treated as an inpatient.

She has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/-
towards medical treatment, conveyance, nourishment and the incidental expenses.
3. Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and she was working as teacher and was earning Rs.12078/- per month.

Due to the accident, she has sustained grievous injuries causing Ipsita Panda vs Go Digit General Insurance Limited on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143983356/

Further it contended that the driver of the car was not possessing valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle and knowingly and willfully entrusted the vehicle to a person who had no valid driving licence.

Perhaps the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ravi v. Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226, has observed thus:
"The purpose of lodging the FIR in motor accident cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.

entities.text: Ravi v. Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquility of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if there is delay, the same deserve to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons.

If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground."
In the case on hand since there is no dispute about the involvement of vehicle in the accident, delay of 30 days, in the light of reasons assigned by the PW.1 and also as mentioned in the Ex.P2,
complaint, it cannot be considered as inordinate.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
16. Issue No.2 :
As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
17. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown her age as 35 years.
She has produced driving licence at Ex.P.22 to prove her age.
As per the driving licence, the date of birth of the petitioner is 28.07.1986.
The accident took place on 11.02.2022.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident was 36 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
18. Further, the petitioner has averred that she was working as teacher in Vibgyor group of schools and was earning Rs.12,078/- per month.
In this regard, she has produced Ex.P23 salary slip for the month of December 2019.
However, she has not produced any document to show the income at the time of accident.
Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e., Rs.15,500/-p.m.
as the accident has been occurred in the year of 2022, for the purpose of assessment of compensation
With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
20.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P-8 and other medical records reveals that in the accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1. Punctured wound present over medial aspect of right foot 1 cm x 0.5 cm x bone deep.
2. Displaced communited fracture of right proximal tibia- plateau with depressed fracture fragments-with intra articular extension info joint with knee effusion and lateral meniscus tear,
Further, the Doctor has opined that injury No.1 is simple in nature and injury No.2 is grievous in nature.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

21.

In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/- under this head.

25.

She further admits that it appears in the bill dated 15.02.2023 that Rs.2,31,221 is due.
Hence Respondent No.1 has summoned the billing and insurance officer of Manipal hospital and examined as RW.2.
He deposed that only Rs.23,122/- has been paid by the petitioner out of bill amount of Rs.2,31,221/- and remaining amount of Rs.2,08,099/- has been paid by Vial New India Insurance company.

Hence,
the petitioner is entitled Rs.23,122/- by rounding off the same, Rs.23,200/- as a compensation under this head.

28. The learned counsel for respondent No.1 argued that no compensation could be awarded towards loss of physical disability as the disability of petitioner do not affect her capacity to work.

29. In this regard he has relied on the judgment reported in MFA.2155/2014 (MV) Dtd.23.06.2020 between Sri.Nandeesh K. Vs. United India Insurance Co.Ltd., and another, wherein High Court Karnataka held as under:
"Damages for loss of earning capacity.

No compensation could be awarded towards loss of earning capacity if physical disability do not affect claimant's capacity to work."
30.
Keeping the aforesaid principles in the mind, this Tribunal considered the evidence on record that whether the physical disability of the petitioner do not affect her capacity to work or not.
In the cross examination of PW.1 it is not elicited that still she is continuing her work or physical disability of the petitioner do not affect her capacity to work.
In fact no question was posed to the PW.1 in this regard.
Under such circumstances, this Tribunal held that respondent No.1 has failed to prove that the physical disability of the claimant do not affect her capacity to work.
31. In the cross-examination, PW.2 has admitted that he is not an Orthopedic.
He further admitted that hip and ankle movements and muscle power of the petitioner is normal.
Fracture is united and implants are not removed.
He admitted that hip and ankle movements and muscle power of the petitioner is normal.
Fracture is united and implants are not removed.
He has assessed permanent disability to the 36% to right leg and 12% to whole body.

Upon careful consideration of the assessment of disability made by PW.2 keeping in mind the fact that PW.1 personally appeared before this court and deposed, also keeping in mind the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 and the treatment which she has taken, Tribunal is of the view that the disability assessed appears to be just and proper.

Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on record and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and by considering the nature of her work, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 12% would be just and proper.
32. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 15.

With multiplier of 15, income of Rs.15,500/- per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to her whole body at 12%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.3,34,800/- (Rs.15,500 x 12 x 15 x 12/100 = Rs.3,34,800/-).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,34,800/- under this head.

35. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending car bearing No.KA-51-AC-4417.
There is no dispute of the fact that the respondent No.1 is the insurer and the respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the driver of the offending vehicle.

36. Now that this court has ascertained the compensation amount, the last aspect of the matter is regarding fixation of liability i.e., who should be made liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner?.
Precisely, it is the specific case of the respondent No.1 that the respondent No.3 who is driver of the offending vehicle at the time of accident had drove the car without driving licence.
In this regard he relied upon the charge sheet and other police documents.

On perusal of the charge sheet, it is crystal clear that after investigation the IO has filed the charge sheet against respondent No.2 and 3 who are the owner and driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279, 338 of IPC, under section 3(a), r/w sec. 181, 5(1) r/w sec. 180 of MV Act holding that the respondent No.3 driver of the offending vehicle had no driving licence at the time of accident.

Further Ex.P.10 reply to the notice under Section 133 of IMV Act given by respondent No.2/owner of the vehicle shows that the Ravika Thomar/driver of the offending vehicle at the time of accident was not having driving licence.

Further Ex.P.15 to 17 order sheet and accusation in CC.No.5972/2022 made it clear that the respondent No.2 and 3 who are the owner and driver of the offending vehicle have admitted guilty and paid penalty stating that driver had no driving licence at the time of accident.
37. For the reasons discussed as supra, it is established that the driver of the offending vehicle bearing registration No.KA-51-AC-4417 was not having valid licence at the time of the accident.
38. The next aspect to be pondered upon now is, what is the effect of the driver of the offending vehicle not possessing a valid driving license at the time of accident.
